📚 Today you learned

OCA vs. OCO — One-Cancels-All Bracket Mechanics

Both your open names sit inside an "OCA" bracket right now — GOOG's TP $408 / stop $333.90, SPXC's exit-limit $205 / stop $186.90. OCA (One-Cancels-All) is IBKR's version of what most brokers call OCO (One-Cancels-Other): a group of orders where filling any one instantly cancels the rest. The distinction matters because OCA groups can hold more than two orders — IBKR lets you stack a TP, a trailing stop, and a hard stop in one group, all racing each other, with only the fastest fill surviving. The failure mode to watch: if you manually cancel or modify one leg of an OCA group, IBKR doesn't always re-link the survivors automatically — check the group is still intact after any hand edit, especially on SPXC where the exit itself is time-sensitive.

Also today: Ex-dividend date — the first day a stock trades without the right to the next declared dividend; buyers on or after that date don't get it. GOOG's is Sept 4.
